title: Delta weight-and-balance system outage briefly halts Atlanta-bound flights
date_note: Fox News says the outage happened on Sunday morning, 22 November, the day of its article; no clock time given.
geo_basis: Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, named by Fox News
summary: An outage of Delta Air Lines' automated weight-and-balance system on Sunday morning led the FAA to briefly halt Atlanta-bound flights, Fox News reported; it said the outage has reportedly delayed at least 3,500 Delta flights across hubs including Atlanta and LaGuardia. Delta told Fox News its teams were using manual workarounds while work continued to restore automation.
plain: A Delta computer system that works out aircraft weight before take-off failed on Sunday morning, and the FAA briefly stopped flights to Atlanta. Fox News said at least 3,500 flights were reportedly delayed.
exec: A failure in one airline system reportedly delayed at least 3,500 Delta flights, Fox News said; expect knock-on delays for staff travel.

evidence.quote: has reportedly delayed at least 3,500 Delta flights across major hubs

key_findings: Delta's automated weight-and-balance system failed on Sunday morning
The FAA briefly halted Atlanta-bound flights
Delta said teams were using manual workarounds

validation.note: One publisher read: Fox News, which quotes Delta's statement on manual workarounds. The 3,500 figure is Fox News' 'reportedly' with no named source. Fox News gives no cause beyond the weight-and-balance system and does not say whether a cyberattack was involved.
